# Known bugs that GoogleSQL's compliance tests (`just compliance`) or BigQuery's answers to
# unverified cases found. Each case gives BigQuery's answer after `!>`, which the emulator does
# not give yet: the case passes while the emulator answers otherwise. Every one of them is to be fixed; a fix fails its case, which then
# moves to the file of its function, written with `=>`.
#
# Inputs come from UNNEST so that the analyzer cannot fold the expression into a constant, which
# it evaluates correctly.

# BigQuery reports where the exception was thrown; QuickJS keeps only where an Error was created.
CREATE TEMP FUNCTION f() RETURNS STRING LANGUAGE js AS "throw new Error('boom');";
SELECT f()
!> error: Error: boom at f() line 1, column 1

# BigQuery snaps a polygon's edges as well as its vertices, which may leave a collection, and snaps
# rings that cross or touch at an edge to where they meet, which may be a new vertex; the
# emulator rejects these.
SELECT ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 1 0, 1.000000000006 0, 1.000000000012 0, 0 1, 0 0))')
!> "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION(LINESTRING(1 0, 1.000000000012 0), POLYGON((0 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0)))"

SELECT ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0), (0.000000000001 0, 0.5 0.1, 0.1 0.5, 0.000000000001 0))')
!> "POLYGON((1e-12 0, 1 0, 0 1, 1e-12 0), (0.1 0.5, 0.5 0.1, 1e-12 0, 0.1 0.5))"

SELECT ST_MAKEPOLYGON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0)'), [ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0.000000000001 0, 0.5 0.1, 0.1 0.5, 0.000000000001 0)')])
!> "POLYGON((1e-12 0, 1 0, 0 1, 1e-12 0), (0.1 0.5, 0.5 0.1, 1e-12 0, 0.1 0.5))"

SELECT ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('POLYGON((0.000000000001 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0.000000000001 0), (0 0, 0.5 0.1, 0.1 0.5, 0 0))')
!> "POLYGON((9.99999999995001e-13 5.0001294663102e-12, 1 0, 0 1, 9.99999999995001e-13 5.0001294663102e-12), (0.1 0.5, 0.5 0.1, 9.99999999995001e-13 5.0001294663102e-12, 0.1 0.5))"

# ST_ASGEOJSON of a line that crosses the antimeridian is unsupported: BigQuery splits it into a
# MULTILINESTRING at longitude 180, in an order these two cases do not settle.
SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(170 0, -170 0)'))
!> "{ \"type\": \"MultiLineString\", \"coordinates\": [ [ [170, 0], [180, 0] ], [ [-180, 0], [-170, 0] ] ] } "

# ST_ASGEOJSON of a line that touches a pole is unsupported: BigQuery stops a line through the
# pole there, and repeats a vertex at the pole.
SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(0 80, 180 80)'))
!> "{ \"type\": \"LineString\", \"coordinates\": [ [0, 80], [2.47425302656506e-30, 85], [7.40392852016821e-30, 87.5], [1.7253895589888e-29, 88.75], [3.69491416784749e-29, 89.375], [7.63372903183229e-29, 89.6875], [1.55112415890358e-28, 89.84375], [3.12662081188226e-28, 89.921875], [6.27761118861833e-28, 89.9609375], [1.25795904774818e-27, 89.98046875], [2.51835483229074e-27, 89.990234375], [5.03914636476199e-27, 89.9951171875], [1.00807294114023e-26, 89.99755859375], [2.01638954955509e-26, 89.998779296875], [4.03302276593581e-26, 89.9993896484375], [8.06628919850318e-26, 89.9996948242188], [1.61328220636626e-25, 89.9998474121094], [3.22658877944806e-25, 89.9999237060547], [3.22658877944806e-25, 90], [0, 90] ] } "

SELECT ST_ASGEOJSON(ST_GEOGFROMTEXT('LINESTRING(30 90, 30 80)'))
!> "{ \"type\": \"LineString\", \"coordinates\": [ [30, 90], [30, 90], [30, 80] ] } "

# BigQuery's COMMIT after a handled error keeps the statements before the error and nothing of the
# statement that failed: https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/transactions. DuckDB aborts the
# transaction on the error and has no savepoints, so the emulator rejects the COMMIT.
CREATE TEMP TABLE committed (n INT64);
BEGIN
  BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  INSERT committed VALUES (1);
  SELECT ERROR('fail');
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM committed
!> "1"

CREATE TEMP TABLE committed (n INT64);
BEGIN
  BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  INSERT committed VALUES (1);
  INSERT committed SELECT IF(n = 3, ERROR('fail'), n) FROM UNNEST([2, 3]) AS n;
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM committed
!> "1"
